blocks.title: Macroscopic events
blocks.text: Macroscopic events are the phenomena that can be observed with the naked eye without considering the individual particles or molecules involved in the process.

A change in colour, the evolution or absorption of heat, the formation of a precipitate, the evolution of a gas, a change in volume or pressure, and a change in the composition of a substance in a chemical reaction are examples of macroscopic properties.

blocks.prompt: A test tube turns warm and a yellow solid settles when two colourless solutions are mixed. Which macroscopic events have been observed?
blocks.explanation: Evolution of heat (the tube warms), a change of colour (colourless to yellow) and the formation of a precipitate (the solid settling) are all macroscopic events, seen without any reference to the ions and molecules that cause them.

items: Macroscopic events are seen with the naked eye: colour change, heat evolved or absorbed, a precipitate, a gas, a change in volume, pressure or composition.
